title: Expiring links and custom aliases
summary: Extend the existing link-creation API with two optional inputs - a lifetime after which the link stops redirecting, and a caller-chosen short code - without changing the behaviour of existing links or of clients that do not use the new inputs.

functional.statement: A client can give a link a lifetime when creating it.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/links accepts optional expires_in_seconds between 60 and 31536000 (365 days)
The response and the metadata endpoint expose the resulting expires_at
A value outside the range or of the wrong type returns 422
From expires_at onwards (inclusive) GET /{code} returns 410 Gone
Refused visits are not counted as clicks
Metadata and statistics of an expired link remain available

functional.statement: A client can choose the short code.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/links accepts optional alias of 3-32 letters, digits, '-' or '_'
The alias is used verbatim as the code and the response marks the link as custom

functional.statement: An alias cannot collide with another link or with the service's own routes.
acceptance_criteria: An alias that is already in use returns 409 and never replaces the existing link
A malformed alias or a reserved name (api, docs, healthz, readyz, ...) returns 422
The code of a deleted link cannot be claimed as an alias

non_functional.statement: Backward compatibility: nothing that works today changes.
acceptance_criteria: Requests without the new fields produce the same result as before
Existing links keep redirecting and never expire
The existing test-suite passes; any test that changes is changed deliberately and listed

non_functional.statement: Safe schema change: the database upgrade is automatic, additive and atomic.
acceptance_criteria: A populated v1 database upgrades in place with no data loss
A failing migration leaves the previous schema untouched
The previous application release still runs against the upgraded schema

assumptions.statement: 'After a set amount of time' means a lifetime relative to creation, supplied in seconds; an absolute timestamp input is not needed.
Aliases live in the same namespace as generated codes and are case-sensitive, like generated codes.
Expiry is not retroactive: links that exist today never expire and cannot be given a lifetime in this change.

out_of_scope: Changing the lifetime or alias of an existing link
Deleting expired links or their analytics
